key_insight: K/Rb double perovskites β2SnGeX6 are predicted by DFT to be stable, ductile, and highly tunable semiconductors whose bandgaps and thermoelectric performance can be engineered by changing the halogen.
engineering_relevance: These lead-free cubic halide double perovskites are promising for photovoltaic absorbers, tandem/near-IR optoelectronics, and high-ZT waste-heat recovery devices.
method: Density functional theory used to study six compositions: K/Rb with Cl/Br/I.
Structural stability assessed via formation energy, tolerance factor, and octahedral factor.
Electronic, optical, elastic, and thermoelectric properties computed from band structures and transport parameters.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct bandgaps tunable from 1.44 to 0.64 eV, ductile elastic behavior across the series, and a peak thermoelectric figure of merit of ZT = 2.4 for K2SnGeI6 at 1000 K.
watch_item: The results are theoretical DFT predictions, so experimental synthesis, defect tolerance, and long-term device stability still need validation.
paper_title: First-Principles Study of Novel Lead-Free Double Perovskite \b{eta}2SnGeX6 (\b{eta} = K, Rb; X = Cl, Br, I) for thermomechanical, optoelectronic and outstanding thermoelectric applications
